program.name: Restack, second call: January 2027

geography.scope: Strong European dimension required. The standard route allocates at least 60% of funds to team members from Horizon Europe-eligible countries; exceptional quality and unique expertise can justify consideration outside those countries.

requirements: Research and development with open-access scientific results and fully open-source software/hardware; submit in English.
Strong European dimension under the published funding-share or exceptional-expertise rules.
First proposals cannot exceed EUR 50,000. Larger proposals require successfully completed Restack or equivalent projects.
Generative AI cannot write proposals except for accessibility support; LLM and diffusion-model use in project development is limited to read-only.
exclusions: GenAI projects are outside scope unless already used by over one million active human users and directly relevant to the stack.

award.note: Standard proposal range; first-proposal ceiling EUR 50,000. Qualified follow-on proposals may reach EUR 150,000; lifetime third-party cap EUR 500,000. EUR 7 million is the programme pool.

application.note: Second call: January 3, 2027 at 12:00 CET (UTC+1). Submit via the official proposal form linked from the call.

supported: Development, testing, security, documentation, accessibility, standardisation, project management and essential infrastructure costs.

evidence.note: Second-call dates, standard award range and GenAI scope.
European dimension, applicant categories and eligible activities.
English proposals, R&D, open outputs and conditional larger awards.

unknowns: Fiscal sponsorship terms; project-specific geographic exception; project duration.
Larger follow-on awards require prior qualifying work and review; they are not the standard first award.

program.name: Delta-based golden mussel decontamination, 2026

geography.scope: Projects on or centrally located to Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta waterways, serving Yolo, Sacramento, Solano, Contra Costa and San Joaquin counties, California.

requirements: Meet the Delta location and five-county service requirements.
Register in CDFW WebGrants and submit under Invasive Mussel Response.
Obtain required permits and site access permissions; cost share is encouraged but not required.

award.note: USD 6 million total programme funding; individual award bounds not established. Reimbursement, with conditional advances for qualified nonprofits and federally recognized Tribes.

application.note: December 15, 2026 at 4 p.m.; schedule says Pacific Time, while sections 1 and 6.1 say PDT despite the winter date. Exact UTC cutoff remains unresolved. Apply in WebGrants.

supported: One-time decontamination equipment, site improvements, staff training and outreach.
excluded: Work before an executed agreement is not reimbursed.

evidence.note: November call guidelines; timing conflict retained. Schedule lists work completion March 15, 2029.
Official registry corroborates date and pool; performance wording differs from call schedule.

unknowns: Exact deadline timezone; individual award range; fiscal sponsorship.
